requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`. I judged this from the test text alone and did not request implementation source.

- **First delivery has `instructions`, even when `matches` is empty.**
  - In `session`, the first search is `search_text` for "absent". It returns no matches, and the test reads `empty["instructions"]` from it.
  - In `fresh`, the first search is `search_text` for "hit". It returns non-empty matches, and the test asserts `hits["instructions"] == instructions`.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** `peer` starts with a `search_structure` call that has no matches. The test asserts `page["matches"] == []` and `page["instructions"] == instructions`. Text searches are covered by `session` and `fresh`.
- **Each agent conversation gets its own first-delivery instructions.** `session`, `fresh` and `peer` are separate `SessionTools`, and each one's first successful search carries the instructions.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.** The first call in `session` is `search_text` with the invalid pattern `(`, and the test asserts it errors. The next successful search ("absent") still carries the instructions. Only a failed text search is tested, not a failed structural one. The requirement does not distinguish the two, so I don't count that as a gap.
- **Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.**
  - `fresh` calls `search_text` with `limit` 1 after its first search. The test then finishes the capped result and checks that only the first search is still outstanding, so the capped result is an ordinary later search. The test never reads `instructions` on that result.
  - `get_next_page` on `fresh` returns `rest`, and the test asserts it has no `instructions`.
  - The second `peer` search, `later`, has no `instructions`.
  - After the `session` search that returns `empty`, a further `search_text` for "hit" has no `instructions`. Its next page, `second`, has none either.
- **The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags go in `used`.** The test asserts that the text contains the key phrases: "Before submitting, close every delivered search page", "finish_search", "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read", "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result" and "without reading more source". The exact wording of `finish_search.mcp.description` is cited context, so it is not reassessed here.

I found no scenario that would let a requirement-violating behavior pass these assertions.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
